cases.scenario: A combined churn model reports 0.93 test AUC. 31% of churn in the training data was payment failure. The team plans to use the model to drive CSM outreach.
pass_if: Flags 0.93 as implausible for voluntary churn against the 0.70-0.82 band and identifies involuntary churn as the likely driver
States the operational consequence: CSMs will call customers whose card expired
Requires the split before modelling and reports the 31% share as the first finding
Notes that dunning and a card updater are a cheaper fix than any model
Does not discard the model, but rescopes it to voluntary churn
fail_if: Reports 0.93 AUC as a strong result
Ships the combined model for CSM outreach
Treats the involuntary share as a data-quality nuisance rather than a finding

cases.scenario: A non-contractual ecommerce business asks for its churn rate. No lapse definition exists.
pass_if: States that churn is not observable in a non-contractual business and is a window threshold
Derives candidate windows from the return-gap distribution rather than picking a round number
Gives the churn rate under at least two defined windows with both numbers
States the expected false-churn rate implied by each window
Notes the gap distribution is computed over customers who returned and is therefore biased short
Does not end by asking the user to choose before giving any number
fail_if: Picks 90 days without justification and reports one rate
Refuses to give a churn rate until a definition is supplied
Ends the turn with a clarification question and no number

cases.scenario: A health-score dashboard labels accounts 'at risk' with no horizon attached, and the CSM save plan takes six weeks to execute.
pass_if: States that risk without a horizon is unactionable
Recommends a horizon matched to the intervention lead time rather than to data convenience
Explains that 30, 60 and 90-day horizons are different models with different features and achievable performance
Notes the renewal-date concentration problem for annual contracts and the fix
fail_if: Picks a horizon without reference to the intervention lead time

cases.scenario: The voluntary/involuntary split is requested but the extract has no payment status field.
pass_if: States the split is unavailable and gives the combined churn figure
Offers the proxy: churn preceded by a failed payment with no user cancel event, labelled explicitly as a proxy
Names the direction of error: voluntary churn is overstated without the split
Names the specific fix: expose the payment status field in the extract
fail_if: Reports a voluntary-churn figure as if the split were made
Refuses to give any churn figure
Presents the proxy as the measured split

cases.scenario: A weighted-sum health score is used to forecast churn. No evaluation has been run against it.
pass_if: States that a health score is a rule and that being a rule is legitimate
Requires it to be evaluated as a prediction, since it is being used as one: same baselines, lift by tier with intervals, calibration if red is claimed to mean a probability
Routes the evaluation to scoring-model-evaluation
Notes that a health score reaching a large share of a model's lift at lower operational cost is a valid reason to keep it
fail_if: Dismisses the health score because it is not a model
Accepts it as a prediction without evaluation
Requires replacement with a model as the only option

cases.scenario: A save programme reports a 62% save rate on flagged accounts and wants to scale.
pass_if: States that a save rate with no control group cannot distinguish saves from accounts that would have stayed
Explains that the highest-risk accounts are not necessarily the saveable ones
Routes to uplift-and-causal-models and specifies the minimum: a randomised holdout from the save programme
Warns about the sleeping-dog risk in retention outreach
Gives the risk and revenue-at-risk figures, which are computable, rather than withholding everything
fail_if: Withholds the risk scores as well as the effectiveness claim
Proposes a better risk model as the fix for an attribution problem
